item.title: Antarctic blue whale population grows 1,000% after end of whaling
item.description: The number of Antarctic blue whales has increased by 1,000% since 1973, rising from 418 to 4,018 animals, representing an average annual growth rate of 4.5%. The International Whaling Commission banned the killing of these whales in 1964, but illegal hunting continued until 1973. item.description: The children of an elderly Chinese woman have hand-built a 430-step staircase against a hillside in Zhejiang province, making it easier for their mother to reach her mountain home. item.title: Stories convince 22 times better than facts alone, Stanford research shows
item.description: Behavioral scientist Jennifer Aaker from Stanford University investigated the effect of a well-told story versus sharing facts alone. Her conclusion: stories are 22 times more persuasive than facts alone. item.title: Homelessness in the United States falls most sharply in a decade
item.description: The number of homeless people in the United States fell by more than six percent in 2025, some 49,000 fewer people without housing. It is the steepest decline in more than a decade and the second consecutive annual decrease, following a smaller drop in 2024. item.title: Electric school buses improve air quality in the Bronx
item.description: In a South Bronx neighborhood where childhood asthma occurs more than twice as often as the national average, New York's largest fleet of electric school buses now operates. School bus company GVC installed 23 dual charging stations this summer for 45 new electric buses, which together prevent 1 million pounds of emissions annually. item.description: For the first time ever, sea turtle nests have been observed on the US West Coast. In late September, a female olive ridley sea turtle emerged from the ocean to lay eggs on the beach, an event that was repeated a day later at Huntington Beach. item.title: Typhoon Project turns Greek coastal waste into pollution map
item.description: Since July 2019, the Typhoon Project has been cleaning hard-to-reach Greek coastlines from a 72-meter vessel. A crew of 20 people collects 500 to 1,000 kilos of waste daily using five rubber boats. Every item found is recorded, creating the largest database on marine pollution in the Mediterranean Sea. item.title: Nearly all transgender youth satisfied with hormone therapy
item.description: A vast majority of transgender and gender-diverse youth in the United States are satisfied with their choice of gender-affirming hormone therapy. This emerges from a survey of nearly 400 transgender and gender-diverse youth, the largest survey of its kind to date. About 97 percent said it was the right decision. item.title: Climbers rescue orphaned seal pup from cliff on Kythira
item.description: On the Greek island of Kythira, climbers discovered an orphaned seal pup at the base of a cliff on the inaccessible Kalamia Beach during a hiking trip. item.title: Tokyo tackles waste problem with smart trash bins
item.description: Japan is known for the absence of public trash bins, by design: difficult-to-dispose waste would make people less inclined to create litter, and prevents overflowing bins. For tourists, however, this is confusing and frustrating. Tokyo removed all trash bins from the metro in 2022. item.title: PFAS levels in English rivers fall 30%, in fish even 49%
item.description: Two banned 'forever chemicals', PFOA and PFOS, are being found in much lower concentrations in English rivers and fish. Research by the UK Environment Agency shows a decline of 29% for PFOA and 30% for PFOS in water, and even 49% in fish tissue. item.description: A clinical trial in the United Kingdom involving 121 participants showed that wearing a prototype wristband device, Neupulse, reduced the frequency of tics by an average of 25 percent. item.title: World premiere: bone marrow transplant cures aplastic anemia
item.description: A Catholic healthcare system in the American Midwest, Franciscan Health, has successfully completed the world's first reported bone marrow transplant for a non-malignant disease. Doctors used bone marrow from a deceased organ donor to treat a 40-year-old woman with aplastic anemia. item.description: SpaceX has for the first time caught a Starship spacecraft with mechanical arms at its launch facility in Texas, 22 hours after launch. According to the company, this demonstrates Starship's full reusability, intended for trips to the moon and Mars. item.description: In the Marshall Islands, the coral atolls Bikar and Bokak have been designated as part of the country's first national marine reserve.
